description: Shows exactly what a chart generation would send to the BIC backend for these arguments - the measured shape of your data (column names, types, counts, ranges), the settings, and whether any sample rows travel - with the credentials removed. SENDS NOTHING and needs no license: it is local and free. Takes the same arguments as a generation. It answers 'what data leaves my machine?'; the eligibility list sends a subset of the same shape.

chart_style.description: Narrows the charts considered to one family: 'traditional' = the familiar forms (bar, stacked and grouped bar, line, area, pie, donut, card, gauge), 'non_traditional' = every other chart type. A chart named in chart_type is still honored unless the data shape disqualifies it, and 'traditional' also turns chart_variety off. Unset considers both families.

chart_type.description: Preferred chart type by name (honored unless the data shape disqualifies it).

chart_variety.description: How much variety the person asks for: the probability, from 0 to 1, that the choice among the charts that fit this data is nudged toward a less conventional one, when the engine runs its planning pass. The nudge is among already-valid charts only: when only the obvious chart honestly fits, it is kept. It has no effect with an explicit chart_type, chart_style 'traditional' or reasoning_mode 1P or CP. Unset: the server's own default.

compactness.description: How roomy the person wants the chart: 'spacious' = roomier margins and more aggressive aggregation of a high-cardinality column, 'balanced' = standard margins and label density, 'compact' = tighter margins and denser axes, aggregating only when cardinality clearly exceeds what fits. Unset: a level is drawn at random for each generation.

csv_path.description: Path to a CSV file (header row required).

culture.description: The caller's language and region as a BCP 47 tag such as 'de-DE', 'fr' or 'ja-JP'. Default 'en-US'. It is the language the chart's own text is written in (titles, axis labels, legends, notes), and it breaks the tie when a CSV's numbers or dates are ambiguous: 12.500 as twelve thousand five hundred or twelve and a half, 05.03.2024 as 5 March or 3 May. Set it from the end user's locale when you know it; it does not translate the data.

data.description: A pre-typed {columns, rows} table — the shape a Fabric DAX query / dataframe already has. Alternative to csv_path/csv_text; when columns carry isMeasure/format/description the shape matches PBI fidelity with no guessing.

dataType.description: Known type (DAX/semantic-model callers have it); omit to infer from values.

description.description: Column description from the model → modelDesc.

format.description: Format string from the model (e.g. "$#,##0") → modelFormat.

isMeasure.description: Known measure/dimension role; omit to apply the numeric-non-identifier heuristic. A semantic-model caller should set this.

rows.description: Rows as positional arrays aligned to columns, OR objects keyed by column name.

data_labels.description: Whether the person wants the value printed on each mark: 'include' asks for the labels, 'exclude' for none. Per-mark labels are suppressed when more than 30 marks would carry one. Unset: the engine decides.

date_grain.description: The time grain the person asks for on the time axis: day, week, month, quarter, year or decade. It is passed on as a strong request, and a different bucket the engine plans is rewritten to it when the dates give that grain 2 or more periods; data with no date column can't honor it. Unset: the engine chooses, from the number of periods the dates give at each grain.

derived_measures.description: Whether the person allows derived measures (ratios, z-scores, percent change, rank, index): 'discourage' keeps the chart to the raw columns (aggregations and sorts still apply); 'encourage' keeps them allowed and rules out the draw that would turn them off, without asking for more of them. Unset: a weighted draw for each generation. 'encourage' is not sent with forbid_derived_columns.

descriptions.description: Per-column human DESCRIPTION — gives the model semantic context the bare column name lacks.

dimensions.description: Columns to treat as DIMENSIONS (a PBI category/axis well — fields to group/break by). Use for numeric codes/years that should NOT be aggregated.

font_family.description: The font family the person names for the chart's own text (titles, axis labels, tick labels, legends), or the one their house style says: a family such as 'Segoe UI' or a stack such as 'Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif'. A font isn't a property of the data or the project. It applies to whichever renderer is chosen, and an unavailable family falls back to a web-safe stack rather than failing. Unset: the engine decides.

forbid_derived_columns.description: True = show only fields present in the data (plus required_columns) — no per-capita, share-of-total, index, rank or z-score columns the engine would otherwise add. Use when your app owns the analytics and the chart is only the display.

formats.description: Per-column number/date FORMAT STRING (e.g. {"Revenue":"$#,##0","Margin":"0.0%"}). PBI supplies these from its model; a CSV can't, so provide them to steer number formatting.

group_by.description: Columns that are the PRIMARY series/breakdown (the PBI 'Group by' well); the backend leads the visualization with these.

group_others.description: Whether the person allows the categories beyond a limit to be grouped into one 'Others' bucket. True is the same as unset: under a limit the rest is grouped and the total stays whole; with no limit the engine decides whether to group. False: the rest is dropped and nothing is grouped. Unset: grouping allowed. group_others true is not sent with rows_policy 'all', which draws every row.

in_chart_caption.description: Whether the person asks for a one-line subtitle under the chart title naming the chart type, any derived measure used and any non-default aggregation. Unset or false: none.

include_code.description: Include the full code in the response — governs BOTH the text block and structuredContent.code. Default: true, or FALSE when out_dir is given (the code is then already on disk, and a large chart's code can overflow a client's tool-output limit). Set it explicitly to override either default.

industry.description: The industry the person names for the data, one of the listed values. A recognized metric name is used only when the columns are that industry's inputs for it. Unset: no industry context is added.

language.description: Project source language: with no concrete `renderer`, javascript/typescript generates D3 (the renderer @bicharts/chart-host draws) and python lets the backend auto-pick within Plotly/matplotlib. Omit to AUTO-DETECT from the working dir.

legend_placement.description: Where the person wants the legend: 'outside' = in the chart margin, 'inside' = within the plot area where it overlaps the data least, 'none' = no standalone legend (the chart's own labels carry the names). A single-series chart draws no legend whichever is chosen. Unset: outside on a chart at least 500 px wide, the renderer's default on a narrower one.

level_of_detail.description: The user's own preference for how much of the data to see, as they've stated it; it isn't a property of the data. 'High' = every observation drawn as its own mark (scatter, beeswarm, strip). 'Medium' = every row used, but shown as a distribution (box, violin, histogram). 'Low' = one mark per category (bars, cards, pies). Unset when the user hasn't stated one; unset is a proven no-op and the engine decides. This is a strong nudge, not a filter: it reorders charts that already fit, and an explicit chart_type still wins.

limit_count.description: How many groups or categories the person asks to keep, from 1 to 10000. The engine keeps exactly that many by the measure, and its own Top-N, 'Other'-cap and cardinality rules yield to it. Unset: no limit from the person (the engine's own Top-N rules still apply).

limit_to.description: The subset the person asks for, passed on as an authoritative instruction to limit to or focus on exactly it: 'latest', 'top' (top / greatest), 'bottom' (bottom / smallest), 'most_common' or 'outliers'. limit_count says how many are kept. Unset: the engine decides.

measures.description: Columns to treat as MEASURES (the PBI 'Values' well — fields the chart aggregates). Numeric non-identifier columns are measures by default.

non_additive.description: MEASURE columns that must NOT be summed (a ratio/average/rate — use mean, never stack). Usually auto-detected; this is an authoritative override.

others_label.description: The name the person gives the 'Others' bucket, at most 40 characters; quotes, backticks and control characters are removed and longer text is cut. Unset: 'Other'. Not sent when group_others is false.

out_dir.description: Optional directory to write chart.js/py, a data.sample.json, and (if preview_html) preview.html.

overlay.description: The analytical layer the person asks for: 'moving_avg' = moving average, 'trend_line' = trend / regression line, 'anomaly' = anomaly highlights, 'confidence_band' = confidence band, 'forecast' = forecast / projection, 'yoy' = year-over-year comparison. It is strongly preferred where it applies to the chosen chart and data (the engine adds the derived measures it needs); where it can't apply, this data can't honor it. Unset: the engine decides.

preview_html.description: Also emit a standalone D3 preview (needs out_dir). Default false — the code is meant to be merged, not run as an index.html.

privacy_level.description: How much detail to compute/share: 0 names only, 10 +counts, 20 +detailed stats (default), 30 +obfuscated sample rows.

project_dir.description: Directory to auto-detect the project language from (default: the folder setup_fabric_app used, else the working directory or the one project folder directly inside it).

prompt.description: Freeform guidance for the generation — the same 'user commentary' lane the Power BI visual uses. Steer encoding/axes/emphasis in plain language, e.g. 'put Year on the x-axis, color by Division', 'render citations as a chord diagram', 'log scale on revenue', 'annotate the peak'.

reasoning_mode.description: LLM pass structure; empty = backend heuristic.

renderer.description: Force a specific renderer (overrides `language`). Omit to use `language`/auto-detection; 'VISUAL'/'' = let the backend choose.

required_columns.description: Fields that MUST be visible in the output, each as its own column/channel. AUTHORITATIVE and VERIFIED: if the generated code never references one, the server regenerates automatically rather than returning a chart that silently dropped it.

rows_policy.description: 'auto' (default) = the engine decides how to summarize. 'all' = render EXACTLY one mark/row per source row, with no Top-N, no 'Other' rollup and no sampling. Use 'all' when your app depends on every row being present (a row-per-entity table, a point per location).

show_title.description: Whether the person wants a title inside the chart: true asks for a concise one, false asks for none. A yes or no, not the title's text. Unset: a chart narrower than 400 px or shorter than 300 px gets none, and a larger one draws at random whether to have one.

wrap.description: Code form: 'none' (default) = the raw render() function to merge; 'esm' = same code plus `export { render };` so the file can be `import`ed. Both forms are accepted everywhere - @bicharts/chart-host strips the export clause before compiling - so this is a convenience, never a compatibility choice.

title: Preview what a request sends
